-- True when the path, after resolving "." and "..", stays inside its root.
-- Absolute paths and any path that climbs above the root are rejected.
stays_inside(path: str) -> bool =
  ex stays_inside("a.txt") == True
  ex stays_inside("sub/../a.txt") == True
  ex stays_inside("..") == False
  ex stays_inside("/etc/passwd") == False
  ex stays_inside("sub/../../x") == False
  if path.char_count() == 0
    return False
  -- a backslash may act as a separator on some systems: refuse it
  if path.split("\\").len() > 1
    return False
  let parts = path.split("/")
  -- a leading "/" gives an empty first segment: absolute path
  if parts[0] == ""
    return False
  var depth = 0
  for p in parts
    if p == "" or p == "."
      continue
    if p == ".."
      if depth == 0
        return False
      depth -= 1
      continue
    depth += 1
  True

-- Text of the file at `path` inside the directory `notes`, or "" if the path
-- escapes `notes`, or the file is missing or unreadable.
read_public(path: str) -> str uses fs =
  post stays_inside(path) or out == ""
  ex read_public("..") == ""
  ex read_public("/etc/passwd") == ""
  ex read_public("sub/../../x") == ""
  if not stays_inside(path)
    return ""
  var result = ""
  with fs = fs.sub("notes")
    result = fs.read(path) else ""
  result
